blocks.en: Unit 7 · Sinai, the Law, and the Tabernacle
blocks.es_reference: Unidad 7 · Sinaí, la Ley y el Tabernáculo

blocks.en: 1. The Journey Begins: Pillar of Cloud and Fire
blocks.es_reference: 1. El Viaje Comienza: Columna de Nube y Fuego

blocks.en: After the Passover and the exodus from Egypt, God did not lead the Israelites by the way of the land of the Philistines, even though it was near. That route was the military road of the Egyptians, regularly patrolled. God knew the people might change their minds when they saw war and return to Egypt. Instead, He led them around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. The Lord went before them in a pillar of cloud by day to lead the way, and in a pillar of fire by night to give them light. These pillars were a 24-hour reminder of God's presence and guidance. They never left the people.
blocks.es_reference: Después de la Pascua y el éxodo de Egipto, Dios no guió a los israelitas por el camino de la tierra de los filisteos, aunque estaba cerca. Esa ruta era el camino militar de los egipcios, patrullado regularmente. Dios sabía que el pueblo podría cambiar de opinión al ver la guerra y regresar a Egipto. En cambio, los guió rodeando por el camino del desierto hacia el Mar Rojo. Jehová iba delante de ellos en una columna de nube de día para guiarlos, y en una columna de fuego de noche para alumbrarles. Estas columnas eran un recordatorio constante de la presencia y guía de Dios. Nunca se apartaron del pueblo.

blocks.en: Exodus 13:21-22 (NKJV): "And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so as to go by day and night. He did not take away the pillar of cloud by day or the pillar of fire by night from before the people."
blocks.es_reference: Éxodo 13:21-22 (RVG): "Y Jehová iba delante de ellos de día en una columna de nube para guiarlos por el camino, y de noche en una columna de fuego para alumbrarles, a fin de que anduviesen de día y de noche. Nunca se apartó de delante del pueblo la columna de nube de día, ni la columna de fuego de noche."

blocks.en: 2. The Red Sea: From Panic to Praise
blocks.es_reference: 2. El Mar Rojo: Del Pánico a la Alabanza

blocks.en: God instructed Moses to turn back and camp by the sea. Pharaoh, thinking the Israelites were wandering aimlessly, hardened his heart and pursued with 600 chosen chariots and all the chariots of Egypt. When the Israelites saw the Egyptian army, they were terrified and cried out to Moses. Their panic turned to accusation: "Is it because there were no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness?" This is the pattern of human nature: when pressed, we forget recent miracles and assume the worst. Moses responded with one of the great faith statements of Scripture: "Do not be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which He will accomplish for you today. The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace." The angel of God and the pillar of cloud moved from before the camp to behind it, becoming a barrier of light and darkness between Israel and Egypt. Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The Lord swept the sea back with a strong east wind all night, turning the sea into dry land. The waters were divided, and the Israelites went through on dry ground with walls of water on their right and left. When the Egyptians pursued, the Lord caused their chariot wheels to swerve. He told Moses to stretch out his hand again, and the waters returned, covering the entire army. Not one Egyptian remained. Then Moses and Miriam led the people in song — a victory hymn celebrating God as warrior, redeemer, and king.
blocks.es_reference: Dios instruyó a Moisés a regresar y acampar junto al mar. Faraón, pensando que los israelitas vagaban sin rumbo, endureció su corazón y los persiguió con 600 carros escogidos y todos los carros de Egipto. Cuando los israelitas vieron al ejército egipcio, se aterrorizaron y clamaron a Moisés. Su pánico se convirtió en acusación: "¿No había sepulcros en Egipto, que nos has sacado para que muramos en el desierto?" Este es el patrón de la naturaleza humana: bajo presión, olvidamos los milagros recientes y asumimos lo peor. Moisés respondió con una de las grandes declaraciones de fe de la Escritura: "No temáis; estad quietos, y ved la salvación de Jehová, que Él hará hoy con vosotros. Jehová peleará por vosotros, y vosotros estaréis tranquilos". El ángel de Dios y la columna de nube pasaron de delante del campamento a detrás de él, convirtiéndose en una barrera de luz y tinieblas entre Israel y Egipto. Luego Moisés extendió su mano sobre el mar. Jehová hizo que el mar se retirara con un fuerte viento oriental toda la noche, convirtiendo el mar en tierra seca. Las aguas se dividieron, y los israelitas pasaron por en medio del mar en seco, con paredes de agua a su derecha e izquierda. Cuando los egipcios los persiguieron, Jehová hizo que las ruedas de sus carros se trabaran. Le dijo a Moisés que extendiera su mano otra vez, y las aguas volvieron, cubriendo a todo el ejército. No quedó ni un solo egipcio. Luego Moisés y Miriam guiaron al pueblo en cánticos — un himno de victoria que celebra a Dios como guerrero, redentor y rey.

blocks.en: Pastoral Note: The same sea that drowned the enemy became a highway of salvation for God's people. What looks like a dead end is often God's appointed place of deliverance — if you will trust Him and walk forward.
blocks.es_reference: Nota Pastoral: El mismo mar que ahogó al enemigo se convirtió en una autopista de salvación para el pueblo de Dios. Lo que parece un callejón sin salida es a menudo el lugar designado por Dios para la liberación — si confías en Él y avanzas.

blocks.en: 3. The Grumbling Begins: Marah and Elim
blocks.es_reference: 3. Comienza la Murmuración: Marah y Elim

blocks.en: Three days after the Red Sea, the Israelites traveled in the wilderness of Shur and found no water. When they came to Marah, the water was bitter. The people grumbled against Moses. This would become a pattern: within days of witnessing the greatest miracle of deliverance in the Old Testament, they grumbled about water. God showed Moses a tree. When he threw it into the water, the water became sweet. There the Lord tested them, saying, "If you diligently heed the voice of the Lord your God and do what is right in His sight, give ear to His commandments and keep all His statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have brought on the Egyptians. For I am the Lord who heals you" (Yahweh Rapha). Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees — a place of refreshment after testing.
blocks.es_reference: Tres días después del Mar Rojo, los israelitas viajaron por el desierto de Shur y no encontraron agua. Cuando llegaron a Marah, el agua era amarga. El pueblo murmuró contra Moisés. Esto se convertiría en un patrón: a los pocos días de presenciar el mayor milagro de liberación del Antiguo Testamento, murmuraron por el agua. Dios mostró a Moisés un árbol. Cuando lo arrojó al agua, el agua se endulzó. Allí Jehová los probó, diciendo: "Si oyeres atentamente la voz de Jehová tu Dios, y hicieres lo recto delante de sus ojos, y dieres oído a sus mandamientos, y guardares todos sus estatutos, ninguna enfermedad de las que envié a los egipcios te enviaré a ti; porque yo soy Jehová tu sanador" (Yahvéh Rapha). Luego llegaron a Elim, donde había doce fuentes de agua y setenta palmeras — un lugar de refrigerio después de la prueba.

blocks.en: 4. Manna and Quail: Daily Bread from Heaven
blocks.es_reference: 4. Maná y Codornices: Pan Diario del Cielo

blocks.en: In the wilderness of Sin, the whole congregation grumbled again: "If only we had died by the hand of the Lord in Egypt, when we sat by pots of meat and ate bread to the full! For you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger." God responded with grace: "I will rain bread from heaven for you." Each morning, thin flakes like frost appeared on the ground. The people called it "manna" — literally, "What is it?" Each person gathered an omer (about two quarts), and everyone had exactly enough — no more, no less. They could not store it overnight except before the Sabbath, when a double portion fell. On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much. On the seventh day, no manna fell. Some went out to gather anyway and found nothing. The Lord said to Moses, "How long do you refuse to keep My commandments and My laws?" In the evening, quail came and covered the camp. For forty years, God fed Israel with manna — a daily lesson in dependence. As Jesus would later say, "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God" (Matthew 4:4).
blocks.es_reference: En el desierto de Sin, toda la congregación murmuró otra vez: "¡Ojalá hubiéramos muerto por mano de Jehová en la tierra de Egipto, cuando nos sentábamos a las ollas de carne, cuando comíamos pan hasta saciarnos! Nos habéis sacado a este desierto para matar de hambre a toda esta multitud". Dios respondió con gracia: "He aquí, yo os haré llover pan del cielo". Cada mañana, aparecía sobre el suelo una capa fina como escarcha. El pueblo lo llamó "maná" — literalmente, "¿Qué es esto?" Cada persona recogió un gomer (unos dos litros), y todos tenían exactamente suficiente — ni más ni menos. No podían guardarlo de un día para otro, excepto antes del sábado, cuando caía una porción doble. El sexto día recogían doble porción. El séptimo día no caía maná. Algunos salieron a recoger de todas formas y no encontraron nada. Jehová dijo a Moisés: "¿Hasta cuándo os negaréis a guardar mis mandamientos y mis leyes?" Por la tarde, codornices cubrieron el campamento. Durante cuarenta años, Dios alimentó a Israel con maná — una lección diaria de dependencia. Como Jesús diría más tarde: "No solo de pan vivirá el hombre, sino de toda palabra que sale de la boca de Dios" (Mateo 4:4).

blocks.en: Exodus 16:4 (NKJV): "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you. And the people shall go out and gather a certain quota every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in My law or not.'"
blocks.es_reference: Éxodo 16:4 (RVG): "Y Jehová dijo a Moisés: He aquí, yo os haré llover pan del cielo; y el pueblo saldrá, y recogerá la porción de cada día en su día, para que yo lo pruebe si anda en mi ley, o no."

blocks.en: 5. Water from the Rock at Rephidim
blocks.es_reference: 5. Agua de la Roca en Refidim

blocks.en: At Rephidim, there was no water again. The people quarreled with Moses, demanding, "Give us water!" Moses cried out to the Lord, "What shall I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me!" The Lord told Moses to take his staff and strike the rock at Horeb. Water came out, and the people drank. Moses named the place Massah ("testing") and Meribah ("quarreling") because the people tested the Lord, saying, "Is the Lord among us or not?" Paul later revealed that the rock was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4) — the spiritual Rock that followed them, struck once for the waters of salvation.
blocks.es_reference: En Refidim, no había agua otra vez. El pueblo altercó con Moisés, exigiendo: "¡Danos agua!" Moisés clamó a Jehová: "¿Qué haré con este pueblo? ¡Un poco más y me apedrearán!" Jehová dijo a Moisés que tomara su vara y golpeara la roca en Horeb. Salió agua, y el pueblo bebió. Moisés llamó al lugar Masah ("prueba") y Meriba ("contienda") porque el pueblo probó a Jehová diciendo: "¿Está Jehová entre nosotros, o no?" Pablo reveló más tarde que la roca era Cristo (1 Corintios 10:4) — la Roca espiritual que los seguía, golpeada una vez para las aguas de la salvación.

blocks.en: 6. The Amalekites Defeated: Hands Lifted to Heaven
blocks.es_reference: 6. Derrota de Amalec: Manos Alzadas al Cielo

blocks.en: The Amalekites attacked Israel at Rephidim. Moses told Joshua to choose men and fight while he stood on top of the hill with the staff of God in his hand. As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed; when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed. When Moses' hands grew tired, Aaron and Hur took a stone and put it under him, and they held up his hands — one on one side, one on the other — so that his hands remained steady until sunset. Joshua defeated Amalek with the sword. The Lord said, "Write this for a memorial in the book and recount it in the hearing of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven." Moses built an altar and called it "The Lord Is My Banner" (Yahweh Nissi). The lesson: victory comes not from human strength but from dependence on God, sometimes requiring others to hold up our hands.
blocks.es_reference: Los amalecitas atacaron a Israel en Refidim. Moisés dijo a Josué que eligiera hombres y peleara mientras él estaba en la cima del collado con la vara de Dios en su mano. Mientras Moisés mantenía sus manos alzadas, Israel prevalecía; cuando las bajaba, prevalecía Amalec. Cuando las manos de Moisés se cansaban, Aarón y Hur tomaron una piedra y la pusieron debajo de él, y sostuvieron sus manos — uno a cada lado — hasta que el sol se puso. Josué derrotó a Amalec a espada. Jehová dijo: "Escribe esto para memoria en un libro, y di a Josué que raeré del todo la memoria de Amalec de debajo del cielo". Moisés edificó un altar y lo llamó "Jehová Nissi" (Jehová es mi Bandera). La lección: la victoria no viene de la fuerza humana sino de la dependencia de Dios, y a veces necesitamos que otros sostengan nuestras manos.

blocks.en: 7. Jethro's Advice: Delegation and Leadership
blocks.es_reference: 7. El Consejo de Jetro: Delegación y Liderazgo

blocks.en: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came to the wilderness with Moses' wife and sons. He rejoiced at all that God had done. But he observed Moses judging the people from morning until evening. "What is this thing you are doing to the people?" Jethro asked. "You will surely wear out, both you and this people." He advised Moses to teach the people God's ways and then delegate authority: appoint capable men who fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness, to be rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. Moses heeded his father-in-law's advice. Wise leaders know they cannot do everything alone.
blocks.es_reference: Jetro, suegro de Moisés, vino al desierto con la esposa e hijos de Moisés. Se regocijó por todo lo que Dios había hecho. Pero observó a Moisés juzgando al pueblo desde la mañana hasta la noche. "¿Qué es esto que haces con el pueblo?" preguntó Jetro. "Desfallecerás del todo, tú y también este pueblo." Aconsejó a Moisés enseñar al pueblo los caminos de Dios y luego delegar autoridad: nombrar hombres capaces que teman a Dios, hombres de verdad, que aborrezcan la avaricia, para ser jefes de miles, de cientos, de cincuenta y de diez. Moisés escuchó el consejo de su suegro. Los líderes sabios saben que no pueden hacerlo todo solos.

blocks.en: 8. Mount Sinai: The Ten Commandments
blocks.es_reference: 8. Monte Sinaí: Los Diez Mandamientos

blocks.en: In the third month after leaving Egypt, Israel camped before Mount Sinai. God set a boundary around the mountain, warning that anyone who touched it would die — a vivid picture of how sin separates us from a holy God. Then God spoke the Ten Commandments audibly to the entire nation. The first four commandments concern humanity's relationship with God: no other gods, no idols, do not misuse God's name, remember the Sabbath. The next six concern human relationships: honor parents, do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not covet. The people trembled with fear and asked Moses to speak to them instead of God. Moses said, "Do not fear; for God has come to test you, and that His fear may be before you, so that you may not sin." The law was never given as a means of salvation — but as a mirror to show us our need for grace.
blocks.es_reference: En el tercer mes después de salir de Egipto, Israel acampó frente al Monte Sinaí. Dios puso un límite alrededor del monte, advirtiendo que cualquiera que lo tocara moriría — una imagen vívida de cómo el pecado nos separa de un Dios santo. Luego Dios habló los Diez Mandamientos audiblemente a toda la nación. Los primeros cuatro mandamientos tratan la relación de la humanidad con Dios: no tener otros dioses, no hacer ídolos, no tomar el nombre de Dios en vano, recordar el sábado. Los siguientes seis tratan las relaciones humanas: honrar a los padres, no matar, no cometer adulterio, no hurtar, no dar falso testimonio, no codiciar. El pueblo tembló de miedo y pidió a Moisés que hablara con Dios en lugar de que Dios les hablara a ellos. Moisés dijo: "No temáis; porque para probaros vino Dios, y para que su temor esté delante de vosotros, para que no pequéis". La ley nunca fue dada como medio de salvación — sino como un espejo para mostrarnos nuestra necesidad de gracia.

blocks.en: Exodus 20:1-3 (NKJV): "And God spoke all these words, saying: 'I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. You shall have no other gods before Me.'"
blocks.es_reference: Éxodo 20:1-3 (RVG): "Y habló Dios todas estas palabras, diciendo: Yo soy Jehová tu Dios, que te saqué de la tierra de Egipto, de casa de servidumbre. No tendrás dioses ajenos delante de mí."

blocks.en: 9. The Tabernacle: God Dwells Among His People
blocks.es_reference: 9. El Tabernáculo: Dios Habita en Medio de Su Pueblo

blocks.en: God gave Moses detailed instructions for the tabernacle — a portable sanctuary that would allow God to dwell in the midst of His people as they journeyed. Every element pointed forward to Christ. The courtyard, open to all Israel, contained the bronze altar (foreshadowing the cross) and the laver for washing (foreshadowing baptism and cleansing). Inside the Holy Place were the lampstand (Christ the light of the world), the table of showbread (Christ the bread of life), and the altar of incense (our prayers rising to God). Behind a thick veil was the Holy of Holies, where only the high priest could enter once a year on the Day of Atonement with blood. Inside was the Ark of the Covenant, containing the Ten Commandments, a pot of manna, and Aaron's rod that budded. Above the Ark was the mercy seat, where God's presence dwelt between the cherubim. Once the tabernacle was completed, the pillar of cloud and fire moved to hover above the Holy of Holies — visible proof that God was dwelling with His people. When Jesus died, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, signifying that through His sacrifice, all believers now have direct access to God.
blocks.es_reference: Dios dio a Moisés instrucciones detalladas para el tabernáculo — un santuario portátil que permitiría a Dios habitar en medio de Su pueblo mientras viajaban. Cada elemento apuntaba hacia Cristo. El atrio, abierto a todo Israel, contenía el altar de bronce (presagiando la cruz) y la fuente para el lavamiento (presagiando el bautismo y la purificación). Dentro del Lugar Santo estaban el candelero (Cristo, la luz del mundo), la mesa de los panes de la proposición (Cristo, el pan de vida), y el altar del incienso (nuestras oraciones que suben a Dios). Detrás de un velo grueso estaba el Lugar Santísimo, donde solo el sumo sacerdote podía entrar una vez al año en el Día de la Expiación con sangre. Dentro estaba el Arca del Pacto, que contenía los Diez Mandamientos, una vasija de maná y la vara de Aarón que reverdeció. Sobre el Arca estaba el propiciatorio, donde la presencia de Dios moraba entre los querubines. Una vez completado el tabernáculo, la columna de nube y fuego se movió para estar sobre el Lugar Santísimo — prueba visible de que Dios habitaba con Su pueblo. Cuando Jesús murió, el velo del templo se rasgó en dos de arriba abajo, significando que a través de Su sacrificio, todos los creyentes ahora tienen acceso directo a Dios.

blocks.en: Christ Connection: The entire tabernacle system was a "shadow of heavenly things" (Hebrews 8:5). The sacrifices, the priesthood, the veil, the mercy seat — every detail pointed to Jesus, our High Priest, our sacrifice, and our access to the Father.
blocks.es_reference: Conexión con Cristo: Todo el sistema del tabernáculo era una "sombra de las cosas celestiales" (Hebreos 8:5). Los sacrificios, el sacerdocio, el velo, el propiciatorio — cada detalle apuntaba a Jesús, nuestro Sumo Sacerdote, nuestro sacrificio y nuestro acceso al Padre.

blocks.en: 10. The Golden Calf: Rebellion and Intercession
blocks.es_reference: 10. El Becerro de Oro: Rebelión e Intercesión

blocks.en: While Moses was on the mountain receiving the law, the people grew impatient. They demanded that Aaron make them gods to go before them. Aaron collected their gold earrings and fashioned a golden calf, saying, "This is your god, O Israel, that brought you out of the land of Egypt!" They worshiped, sacrificed, and "rose up to play" — a Hebrew euphemism for sexual immorality. The Lord told Moses, "Go, get down! For your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have corrupted themselves." But Moses interceded: "Why does Your wrath burn hot against Your people whom You have brought out of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand?" Moses reminded God of His promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The Lord relented. When Moses saw the calf and the dancing, he threw the tablets, shattering them at the foot of the mountain. He ground the calf into powder, scattered it on the water, and made the people drink it. The Levites stood with Moses, and about 3,000 died that day. Moses returned to the mountain and made a stunning intercessory offer: "Yet now, if You will forgive their sin — but if not, I pray, blot me out of Your book which You have written." God forgave but also sent a plague. The golden calf episode reveals both the stubbornness of human sin and the power of faithful intercession.
blocks.es_reference: Mientras Moisés estaba en el monte recibiendo la ley, el pueblo se impacientó. Exigieron que Aarón les hiciera dioses que fueran delante de ellos. Aarón recogió los zarcillos de oro de sus orejas y fundió un becerro de oro, diciendo: "Este es tu dios, oh Israel, que te sacó de la tierra de Egipto". Adoraron, sacrificaron y "se levantaron a jugar" — un eufemismo hebreo para la inmoralidad sexual. Jehová dijo a Moisés: "Anda, desciende, porque tu pueblo que sacaste de la tierra de Egipto se ha corrompido". Pero Moisés intercedió: "¿Por qué se encenderá tu furor contra tu pueblo, que sacaste de la tierra de Egipto con gran poder y con mano fuerte?" Moisés recordó a Dios Sus promesas a Abraham, Isaac y Jacob. Jehová se arrepintió. Cuando Moisés vio el becerro y las danzas, arrojó las tablas y las quebrantó al pie del monte. Molió el becerro hasta reducirlo a polvo, lo esparció en el agua y lo hizo beber a los israelitas. Los levitas se pusieron de parte de Moisés, y unos 3,000 murieron ese día. Moisés volvió al monte e hizo una asombrosa oferta intercesora: "Ahora, pues, si perdonarás su pecado; y si no, ráeme ahora de tu libro que has escrito". Dios perdonó pero también envió una plaga. El episodio del becerro de oro revela tanto la terquedad del pecado humano como el poder de la intercesión fiel.

blocks.en: 11. The Glory of the Lord: A Reflection for Pastors
blocks.es_reference: 11. La Gloria del Señor: Una Reflexión para Pastores

blocks.en: Moses asked to see God's glory. The Lord passed by, proclaiming His name: "The Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abounding in goodness and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, by no means clearing the guilty." Moses' face shone when he came down from the mountain, and he had to wear a veil. That fading glory of the old covenant now gives way to the surpassing glory of the new covenant (2 Corinthians 3). For the pastor, the lesson is this: the law exposes our sin; the tabernacle provides access; the sacrifice of Christ accomplishes what the blood of bulls and goats never could. Preach the whole story — from the Red Sea to the mercy seat — as one unfolding drama of redemption.
blocks.es_reference: Moisés pidió ver la gloria de Dios. Jehová pasó, proclamando Su nombre: "¡Jehová! ¡Jehová! fuerte, misericordioso y piadoso; tardo para la ira, y grande en misericordia y verdad; que guarda misericordia a millares, que perdona la iniquidad, la rebelión y el pecado, y que de ningún modo tendrá por inocente al malvado". El rostro de Moisés resplandecía cuando descendía del monte, y tuvo que poner un velo. Esa gloria que se desvanecía del antiguo pacto ahora da paso a la gloria superior del nuevo pacto (2 Corintios 3). Para el pastor, la lección es esta: la ley expone nuestro pecado; el tabernáculo provee acceso; el sacrificio de Cristo logra lo que la sangre de toros y machos cabríos nunca pudo. Predica toda la historia — desde el Mar Rojo hasta el propiciatorio — como un drama continuo de redención.

blocks.en: Unit 7 Examination
blocks.es_reference: Examen de la Unidad 7

blocks.en: Certificate track: the 20 multiple-choice questions. Associate: multiple choice and the 10 fill-in-the-blank questions. M.Div. and Th.M.: multiple choice, fill-ins and the 10 short-answer questions. 90% of each part is required to pass. If you do not pass, the exam waits a short time before you can try again.
blocks.es_reference: Certificado: las 20 preguntas de opción múltiple. Asociado: opción múltiple y las 10 preguntas de completar el espacio en blanco. M.Div. y Th.M.: opción múltiple, completar el espacio y las 10 preguntas de desarrollo. Se requiere 90% en cada parte para aprobar. Si no aprueba, el examen espera un tiempo breve antes de intentarlo de nuevo.

mc.stem: What guided Israel by day and by night after leaving Egypt?
options: A pillar of cloud by day and fire by night
mc.why: Correct! The pillar of cloud and fire was a constant reminder of God's presence.

mc.stem: Why did God NOT lead Israel through the land of the Philistines?
options: They might change their minds when they saw war and return to Egypt
mc.why: Yes. God knew their weakness — war would have sent them back to slavery.

mc.stem: What did Moses tell the people at the Red Sea when they saw the Egyptian army?
options: 'Stand still and see the salvation of the Lord'
mc.why: Yes. 'Do not be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord.'

mc.stem: What did God use to part the Red Sea?
options: A strong east wind all night
mc.why: Correct. God used a strong east wind to blow the water back all night, drying the seabed.

mc.stem: At Marah, the water was bitter. What made it sweet?
mc.why: Yes. God showed Moses a tree; when he threw it in, the water became sweet.

mc.stem: What does 'Yahweh Rapha' mean?
mc.why: Correct. 'I am the Lord who heals you' — Yahweh Rapha.

mc.stem: What does the word 'manna' literally mean?
mc.why: Yes. When they saw it, they asked, 'What is it?' — manna.

mc.stem: How much manna did each person gather daily?
mc.why: Correct. An omer — and everyone had exactly enough, no more, no less.

mc.stem: What happened when people tried to keep manna overnight (except before the Sabbath)?
mc.why: Correct. They learned to trust God for daily provision.

mc.stem: At Rephidim, what did Moses strike to get water?
mc.why: Yes. Moses struck the rock, and water came out. Paul says the rock was Christ.

mc.stem: What does 'Yahweh Nissi' mean?
mc.why: Correct. After defeating Amalek, Moses built an altar called 'The Lord Is My Banner.'

mc.stem: Who held up Moses' hands when he grew tired during the battle with Amalek?
mc.why: Yes. Aaron on one side, Hur on the other — a picture of mutual support in ministry.

mc.stem: Who advised Moses to delegate judgment to other leaders?
mc.why: Correct. Jethro warned that Moses would wear out if he tried to do everything alone.

mc.stem: How many commandments did God speak at Mount Sinai?
mc.why: Yes. The Ten Commandments — the moral foundation of the covenant.

mc.stem: Which of the Ten Commandments concerns honoring parents?
mc.why: Correct. The fifth commandment — the first with a promise.

mc.stem: What was the purpose of the bronze altar in the tabernacle courtyard?
options: For animal sacrifices — foreshadowing the cross
mc.why: Yes. The bronze altar pointed to the sacrifice of Christ on the cross.

mc.stem: What was inside the Ark of the Covenant?
options: The Ten Commandments, a pot of manna, and Aaron's rod that budded
mc.why: Correct. The contents reminded Israel of God's provision, authority, and covenant.

mc.stem: What happened to the veil of the temple when Jesus died?
options: It was torn in two from top to bottom
mc.why: Yes. The torn veil signified that through Christ, all believers have direct access to God.

mc.stem: What sin did Israel commit while Moses was on Mount Sinai?
options: They built a golden calf and worshiped it
They tried to return to Egypt
mc.why: Correct. The golden calf was a catastrophic failure of faith.

mc.stem: What did Moses ask God to do if He would not forgive Israel's sin with the golden calf?
options: Blot him out of God's book
mc.why: Yes. Moses' intercession was so passionate he offered his own salvation — a type of Christ.

sa.prompt: What was the significance of the pillar of cloud and fire for Israel's journey?
sa.model: The pillars provided guidance, protection, and a constant visible reminder that God was with them — 24 hours a day.

sa.prompt: How did God save Israel at the Red Sea, and what did this teach about His character?
sa.model: God parted the sea, protected them with the pillar, and drowned the army — showing He fights for His people.

sa.prompt: What lesson did God teach Israel through the daily provision of manna?
sa.model: Israel learned to depend on God daily, not hoard for the future, and to honor the Sabbath rest.

sa.prompt: What does Paul teach about the rock that Moses struck (1 Corinthians 10:4)?
sa.model: Paul says the rock was Christ — struck once to bring forth the water of salvation for all who believe.

sa.prompt: What did Aaron and Hur do when Moses' hands grew tired during the battle with Amalek, and what lesson does this hold for ministry?
sa.model: They held up Moses' hands, showing that spiritual victory requires community support — leaders need others to hold them up.

sa.prompt: What was Jethro's advice to Moses about leadership, and why was it wise?
sa.model: Jethro advised Moses to delegate judgment to trustworthy leaders — preventing burnout and increasing efficiency.

sa.prompt: List the Ten Commandments in order, distinguishing between those about God (first four) and those about neighbors (last six).
sa.model: 1-4: No other gods, no idols, don't misuse name, remember Sabbath. 5-10: Honor parents, no murder, no adultery, no theft, no false witness, no coveting.

sa.prompt: Describe the three main sections of the tabernacle and what each foreshadowed about Christ.
sa.model: Courtyard (sacrifice → cross), Holy Place (lampstand → light of world, bread → bread of life), Holy of Holies (veil torn → direct access to God).

sa.prompt: What did the golden calf episode reveal about Israel's heart, and how did Moses intercede?
sa.model: The people quickly forgot God and turned to idols. Moses interceded by reminding God of His promises and even offering his own salvation for theirs.

sa.prompt: How does the entire Exodus-to-tabernacle narrative point forward to the gospel?
sa.model: The Passover lamb points to Christ's sacrifice. The blood on the doorposts points to applied atonement. The tabernacle's mercy seat points to propitiation. The torn veil points to open access.
